data.name: Jauhar
data.gender_notes: Jauhar is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is glowing with inner light and passion. Derived from the word 'jawhar' which means 'complete' or 'whole'. The name Jauhar carries the meaning “Glowing, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Jauhar usually hope their child will grow to embody glowing, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the inner light and passion that every soul possesses. It is a reminder to let your light shine bright and to protect and nurture the fire within you.
data.etymology: Jauhar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Glowing, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jauhar total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_arabic.name: جوهَر
in_arabic.long_meaning: جوهَر مشتق من الجذر العربي جهر الذي يعني الإشراق والضياء، وهو مصطلح يستخدم في الإسلام لوصف نور الله وضياء وجهه، ويحمل هذا الاسم معنىً روحياً عميقاً يتعلق bằng نور الله وبركته

in_urdu.name: جَوہَر
in_urdu.long_meaning: جَوہَر عربی جڑ جھر سے ماخوذ ہے جس کا معنی ہے چمکنا اور روشنی، یہ اسلامی روایت میں الله کے نور اور چہرے کی روشنی کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے، اور یہ نام روحانی طور پر گہرا معنی رکھتا ہے جو الله کے نور اور برکت سے متعلق ہے

in_hindi.name: जौहर
in_hindi.long_meaning: जौहर अरबी मूल जहर से लिया गया है जिसका अर्थ है चमकना और प्रकाश، यह इस्लामी परंपरा में الله के प्रकाश और मुखमंडल की प्रभा के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है, और यह नाम आध्यात्मिक रूप से गहरा अर्थ रखता है जो الله के प्रकाश और कृपा से संबंधित है

in_pashto.name: جوهَر
in_pashto.long_meaning: جوهَر د عربی ریښ جهر څخه اخیستل شوی دی چې معنی یې ځلیدل او رڼا دی، دا اسلامي دود کی الله تعالی د رڼا او چېرې د رڼا لپاره کارول کیږي، او دا نوم روحاني پلوه غړ دی چې الله د رڼا او برکت سره تړاو لري

in_english.name: Jauhar
in_english.long_meaning: Jauhar is derived from the Arabic root jahr, meaning to shine and radiate, it is a term used in Islamic tradition to describe the light of Allah and the radiance of His face, and this name carries a deep spiritual meaning related to the light and blessings of Allah

data.cultural_impact: In the historical context, Jauhar is most commonly associated with the Siege of Chittorgarh, an event in the 14th century during which thousands of women took their lives in order to preserve their honor before falling into the hands of the enemy. The Jauhar tradition symbolizes the immense courage and sacrifice of these women, who chose to die rather than succumb to the invaders. It continues to inspire and fascinate people through various forms of media, such as literature and films.
data.spiritual_significance: Jauhar, etymologically derived from the Arabic word 'jawhar' (complete or whole), represents the idea of transforming oneself into a state of spiritual completeness through the purification of the soul. It's a metaphor for the individual's quest for an inner light, which ultimately leads to a state of inner peace and unity with the divine. By committing to this spiritual journey, one aims to embody the essence of Jauhar - total devotion, selflessness, and the pursuit of inner illumination.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Glowing, Radiant" symbolizes One who is glowing with inner light and passion. Derived from the word 'jawhar' which means 'complete' or 'whole'.. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Jauhar serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of glowing, radiant.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The name Jauhar is mentioned in the book 'The History of the Barmakids' as a term for a type of treasure.
historical_references.context: The name Jauhar was used to describe a collection of precious items seized by the Abbasid Caliphate.

trends: increasing popularity in the Middle East and North Africa
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Jauhar remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: A successful entrepreneur named Zainab Jauhar in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia attributes much of their success to the blessing of their name Jauhar, which means "Glowing, Radiant". They believe their name has shaped their identity and guided them through life.
